results.question: How much revenue did our dresses bring in?

results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * l.quantity) / nullif(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 0) * 100, 2) AS gross_profit_margin_pct FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32% for the period from October 2025 through September 2026. This is calculated from all non-voided orders using ex-GST revenue and costs. Please note that this calculation excludes any product variants that were missing cost data.
results.assumptions: Calculated overall gross profit margin across all non-voided orders for the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Revenue is taken ex-GST (divided by 1.1) after line-level discounts, minus total ex-GST cost (variants.cost * quantity). Variants with NULL cost are excluded.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?

results.answer: Your top 5 products by gross profit are the One-Piece Swimsuit ($165,884.48), Shirt Dress ($130,441.22), Straw Hat ($108,854.01), High-Rise Jeans ($104,531.12), and Wool Coat ($89,912.11). This covers all non-voided orders from October 2025 through September 2026. Please note that any product variants with missing cost data were excluded from these calculations.
results.assumptions: Calculated gross profit as (revenue after discounts ex-GST) minus (unit cost * quantity) for all non-voided orders across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Variants with NULL cost were excluded.

WITH eofy_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'EOFY Sale (19 Jun - 5 Jul)' AS period,
    COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) AS revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  rows WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-06-19'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-07-06'
),
pre_eofy_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'Pre-EOFY (2 Jun - 18 Jun)' AS period,
    COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) AS revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-06-02'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-06-19'
)
SELECT period, revenue, order_count FROM eofy_period
UNION ALL
SELECT period, revenue, order_count FROM pre_eofy_period;
results.answer: Revenue during the EOFY sale jumped to $246,002.91 across 1,240 orders, compared to $186,171.83 from 794 orders in the preceding 17 days. This comparison assumes that the 17-day pre-sale period is a fair baseline for normal trading activity, though seasonal shopping habits may have naturally influenced the lift.
results.assumptions: Compared revenue and order counts for the EOFY sale period (19 June to 5 July 2026, 17 days inclusive) against the immediately preceding 17-day period (2 June to 18 June 2026). Voided orders are excluded.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?
results.sql: SELECT p.title, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v USING (product_id) JOIN order_lines l USING (variant_id) JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold ASC LIMIT 3;
results.answer: The three products that sold the fewest units between October 2025 and September 2026 are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These figures cover all non-voided orders across the entire date range.
results.assumptions: Interpreting units sold as total quantity ordered across all non-voided orders for the entire date range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id HAVING count(order_id) >= 3) t
results.answer: A total of 1,640 registered customers have placed 3 or more non-voided orders. This count is based on the entire data period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. Please note that guest orders without a customer ID are excluded from this total.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: How many registered customers have placed 3 or more non-voided orders across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Guest orders (customer_id IS NULL) are excluded since they cannot be grouped by customer.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation looks at the time difference between the order date and the refund date across all available refund events. Note that this average assumes all relevant refund records were successfully captured in the dataset.
results.assumptions: Calculated the average time difference in days between the order creation date and the refund creation date for all refund events across the entire dataset.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue_with_discount FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND discount_id IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Orders that used a discount brought in a total of $944,363.46 in revenue. This calculation includes both applied discount codes and automatic store-wide sales, while excluding any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Revenue is defined as orders.total for non-voided orders. Orders that used a discount are identified by having a non-null discount_id, which covers both automatic store-wide sales and applied discount codes.

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' AND v.color IS NOT NULL GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Camel was your top-selling color in the winter of 2026, with a total of 1,050 units sold. This count excludes any voided orders, based on your store's local timezone.
results.assumptions: Winter is defined as June, July, and August 2026 based on the store's timezone (Australia/Sydney). Revenue and units exclude voided orders.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM (orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, ROUND(SUM(orders.total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE orders.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM (orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END ORDER BY revenue DESC;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more money than weekends, with weekdays generating 2,147,980.22 AUD and weekends generating 1,173,950.49 AUD. This comparison covers the entire dataset from October 2025 to September 2026, using local Sydney time and excluding voided orders. Since there are five weekdays compared to only two weekend days, the higher weekday total reflects the longer span of time.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Compare total revenue between weekends (Saturday and Sunday) and weekdays (Monday through Friday) using Australia/Sydney local time, excluding voided orders, across the entire date range of the dataset (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026).

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: SELECT product_type, product_title, total_units FROM (SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS total_units, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(l.quantity) DESC) AS rn FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type), p.title) t WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY total_units DESC;
results.answer: Your top-selling items by product type range from the One-Piece Swimsuit leading swimwear with 4,043 units down to the Merino Crew Jumper leading knitwear with 526 units. These figures cover all non-voided orders between October 2025 and September 2026. This data assumes all product types were correctly labelled in the system during this period.
results.assumptions: Calculated total units sold per product within each product type for all non-voided orders across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Product types are normalised to lowercase.

results.question: How many orders contained more than one unit in total?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS multi_unit_orders FROM (SELECT o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING sum(l.quantity) > 1) t
results.answer: There were 8,908 orders that contained more than one unit in total. This count excludes any voided orders based on the data provided.
results.assumptions: Counting distinct orders that have a total quantity greater than one across all order lines, excluding voided orders.
